angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 352,024 km at 117.53 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.5081 +/- 0.0240 mas (same row, RUWE 1.12): 117.53 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.506 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Fukuda et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1883 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026PASJ...78.1602F/abstract): 352,024 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.495 +/- 0.011 solar masses from Fukuda et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1883 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026PASJ...78.1602F/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3554 +/- 26 K from Fukuda et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1883 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026PASJ...78.1602F/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Fukuda et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1883 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026PASJ...78.1602F/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1883.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.724, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1883 (pscomppars): spectral type M, from Peláez-Torres et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A..62P/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, TOI-1883: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1883 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.32 dex, from Fukuda et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026PASJ...78.1602F/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1883 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.43063, from Fukuda et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026PASJ...78.1602F/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 5735744144510573696, flags_flame 00: age_flame 12.267841 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 5.223159 to 13.5)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1883 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 3 km/s, from Fukuda et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026PASJ...78.1602F/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
